deliverables: Ongoing maintenance including bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases
Dijkstra developer preview with initial Plutus V4 support in compiler and standard library
Dijkstra ledger rules and transaction-builder updates including new builtins, cost models, nested transactions, accounts, and guard scripts
Improved JS/TS interfaces and documentation for components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Java/Kotlin integration examples for Spring Boot and Ktor and cleaner integration with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci
Application runtime foundational components, reactive workers, chain follower, and task scheduler
request.what: Funding for a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard fork readiness, interoperability across JVM and JS/TS ecosystems, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is an open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
Scalus is used directly by Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm.
Scalus components are reused in MeshJS SDK, Evolution SDK, Lucid Evolution, Cardano Client Lib, and YaciDevKit.
The project has delivered 4,642 commits across 32 releases with 12 contributors and Scalus.js has more than 20,000 monthly downloads.
The proposal reduces the prior Scalus request from ₳8.503M over 12 months to about ₳2.464844M over 9 months, with FTE reduced from 8.25 to 2.25 and no contingency.
The funded scope excludes a standalone production JVM L1 node, full Gummiworm L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion.

The proposal says Dijkstra readiness is needed because Plutus V4, nested transactions, guard script types, and accounts affect smart contract development, evaluation, transaction building, ledger rules, testing, and workflows.
Delivery is described as milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.
Lantr commits to public reporting, open community sessions showcasing shipped work, and on-time milestone delivery for treasury-funded work.
The proposal frames Scalus as shared Apache 2.0 open-source infrastructure intended to reduce repeated assembly work across Cardano teams and tools.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus from July 2026 through March 2027, focusing on maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a scoped application runtime, with claimed existing ecosystem use, reduced scope versus a prior proposal, milestone governance, and third-party assurance.
